source.title: Learning Capacity: A Measure of the Effective Dimensionality of a Model
source.authors: Dai-Wei Chen; Wei-Di Chang; Pratik Chaudhari

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper explicitly reproduces model-size double descent on ResNet18 and reports model-size sweeps with test loss or test error. It also tests whether plotting test loss against its proposed effective-capacity measure yields double descent.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for model-size sweeps and test loss versus learning capacity. It also reports that average energy/test loss decreases monotonically with sample size, but does not identify whether those sample sizes are near an interpolation threshold, so that result is not recorded as testing V3. The paper discusses but does not measure epoch-wise double descent, peak location prediction by a single complexity measure, noise/regularization dependence, or broad double descent across model classes.
record.test_reason: The paper reproduces model-size double descent (FCNs on MNIST, ResNet18 on noisy CIFAR-10), which bears on V1. It then argues double descent is an artifact of counting bare parameters, because test loss plotted against its learning-capacity measure shows no double descent. That is a specific argument restating V7. The V1 sweeps reproduce the original setup only as context, so T5 fits the paper's main double-descent contribution better than T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors further claim that plotting against learning capacity 'eliminates' double descent: test loss grows with capacity at small N and saturates at large N, rather than tracing a U. They attribute the missing U to learning capacity measuring only the SGD-reachable subset of models.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses model-size sweeps to demonstrate double descent, including an explicitly described reproduction on ResNet18, and adds a learning-capacity analysis. The text does not establish that every size-sweep detail matches the original procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The double-descent demonstration on ResNet18 is reported with CIFAR-10 label noise rate 0.2. The relationship between test loss and learning capacity differs in statistical significance at N = 50,000 from the smaller reported sample sizes.
record.problems: The size-sweep curves and their peaks are presented as figures without numerical peak values or an explicit check of where training-set interpolation occurs. The N = 50,000 learning-capacity slope is reported as not significant, with no exact p-value stated. No controls are reported for these sweeps.

untested.parts: Whether the peak sits near the size that just fits the training set; training error and the interpolation point are not reported.
Test loss falls monotonically with N (Fig. 2), but no sample sweep near an interpolation threshold is done.
Random forests and k-NN are analysed for learning capacity only; no capacity sweep past interpolation is run.
Learning capacity is not used to predict peak location on any axis.
A single noise rate (0.2) is used; no noise or regularization comparison is made.
Only FCNs on MNIST and ResNet18 on noisy CIFAR-10 are tested; other model classes are not.

missing.what: Test loss versus learning capacity for ResNet18 on 0.2-noise CIFAR-10. The caption says double descent is absent there as well, with learning capacity estimated on the noisy data.
missing.locator: Figure 4(b) right panel; Appendix D note

record.verdict_notes: Each learning-capacity curve spans models of different size at fixed N, so the V7 comparison changes both the x-axis and how complexity is estimated; there are no controls. The V1 evidence is figure-only, and the study is not an original source for any version.

versions.untested_parts: The reported size sweeps show double descent, but the paper does not state or measure whether the peak is near the size at which the model just fits the training set.
No test-error sweep over training epochs is reported.
The paper varies sample size and reports decreasing test loss, but does not locate or test the region near an interpolation threshold.
The paper includes non-deep models in learning-capacity experiments, but does not test a double-descent curve across model classes past an interpolation point.
The paper proposes learning capacity as effective dimensionality, but does not test whether one measure predicts peak locations along size, epochs, and sample-size axes.
The paper uses a CIFAR-10 noise rate of 0.2 for one size sweep, but does not compare noise or regularization conditions or test peak splitting or disappearance.
The paper tests its learning-capacity measure on the reported MNIST networks; it does not establish that this measure is an appropriate effective parameter count for every model class.

rows.subject: One- and two-layer fully-connected networks
rows.operation_detail: Sweep network size and measure test loss against number of weights.
rows.measure: Test loss versus number of weights
rows.note: The paper describes this as a double-descent curve; the figure reports the sweep across the fully-connected networks.
rows.check: Figure-only result. The authors label it double descent, but no peak values or interpolation point are given. The subject matches Fig. 4(a) left: one- and two-layer FCNs, 10–100 hidden neurons, N=50,000.

rows.subject: ResNet18

rows.locator: Figure 4, ResNet18 width sweep; Appendix D
rows.note: The paper says this experiment reproduces double descent and identifies the noise rate as 0.2.
rows.check: Figure-only result. The caption calls this panel '(a) Right' while the panel label reads '(b) ResNet-18 on CIFAR10'. The locator should say Fig. 4 ResNet-18 test error vs width. The 0.2 label noise is stated in Appendix D.

rows.subject: FC1 (hidden sizes 10–100) and LeNet
rows.operation_detail: Plot test loss against learning capacity across networks for sample sizes N = 200, 1,000, 2,000, 4,000, and 10,000.
rows.measure: Test loss as a function of learning capacity C
rows.note: Reported result across the plotted networks and listed sample-size conditions: the relationship is monotonic rather than an ordinary U-shaped curve.
rows.check: The subject is wrong: the Section 3.2 and Fig. 4 text describes only fully-connected networks (10–100 hidden neurons) on MNIST, and LeNet is not mentioned. The state should be partial, not absent: the second descent vanishes against learning capacity, but the curve is monotonically increasing, not the U shape V7 predicts. The authors call it 'akin to the later half' of the U.
